reason: οἰκεῖος Σόφακος here denotes a relative of Syphax, not merely a friend.
Chapter seam: the sentence continues in 15.6 (ὑδρείαν ἐντὸς βέλους ποιησάμενος); the English rightly completes it.

fix: And they did not, as even tyrants do, put forward some small pretext to veil their shame
reason: καθάπερ οἱ τύραννοι: tyrants do offer a pretext; current English can be read as the reverse.

fix: For indeed, in this respect Fortune plainly cooperated with Philip.
reason: αὐτῷ συνήργησε means 'worked with him'; 'against' inverts the dative. Any irony is left to the reader.

fix: the Rhodians could not believe it because the faithlessness was so extreme
reason: μὴ δύνασθαι πιστεῦσαι: they were unable to believe it, not 'hardly'. Minimal change keeps the existing wording.

fix: All this happened before the deliberation at Philip’s court [...], as I have said
reason: Lacuna (***) after διαβουλίου must be marked; παρὰ Φιλίππῳ διαβούλιον is a deliberation at his court. ἐδηλώσαμεν kept as 'said'.

fix: the knowledge that delay told against themselves, because Tlepolemus and his party controlled all the supplies being brought into Alexandria
reason: τὸ μέλλειν καθ᾽ αὑτῶν means delay hurt them; the subject of κρατεῖν, τοὺς περὶ τὸν Τληπόλεμον, is at the start of 15.27 and is missing from the ch. 27 English.
